stories.headline: Diggs Rides Home to Washington and Somebody's Cut of the Throws Just Got Thinner
stories.read: Stefon Diggs is signing with the Commanders on a one-year deal worth up to twelve million, which puts a Maryland boy back on his home range lining up opposite Terry McLaurin. Now hold up before you go celebrating, pardner. Diggs caught 85 balls for a thousand yards in New England last year, so the fella can still hunt, and Jayden Daniels throwing him the mail is a considerable upgrade over what he had. But every throw Diggs collects comes out of somebody else's saddlebag, and the young pass-catchers behind McLaurin just turned into dry wells overnight. Doc's play: McLaurin holds his ground, Diggs is cheap gold at a price the saloon hasn't adjusted yet, and anybody else in that Washington receiver room goes back in the bin.

stories.headline: Bijan Gets Paid, Puts the Pads Back On, and the Whole Standoff Ends
stories.read: Atlanta backed up the wagon and handed Bijan Robinson a three-year extension through 2030, roughly sixty-seven million with fifty-one guaranteed, which makes him the best-paid ball-carrier in the territory. He spent the first week of camp standing on the sideline with his arms folded, and now that's over. Here's what matters to your outfit: every nervous fella who was quietly sliding Bijan down his board over the hold-in has no excuse left, and the discount is closing fast. If somebody in your league is still spooked, go swap horses with him today before the news catches up. Tyler Allgeier stays a spare horse worth stabling, nothing more.

stories.headline: Tank Dell Is Back on the Range and Nobody in Your Saloon Is Paying Attention
stories.read: Houston cleared Tank Dell for camp, no PUP list, and the little fella has been running routes and catching mail from C.J. Stroud after losing an entire season to a wrecked knee. Caserio says a short ramp-up and then he's all the way back. Now listen close, because this is the exact shape of a diamond in the rough: a proven pass-catcher, a full year off the ledger so the herd's forgotten his name, and a price in the late rounds that ain't worth arguing over. He was tied to Stroud for real production before the spill. Doc says you spend a cheap dart on him and let the rest of the outfit fight over receivers they already know about.
